meta.parties: Pedris Et Al. v. Batcha Et Al

rules.statement: Under the Roman-Dutch law, a cause of action for lateral support arises only when damage has occurred and not merely due to apprehension of future damage.
rules.supporting_quote: "The underlying principle being that a landowner may lawfully dig upon his own ground to any depth he pleases, provided he causes no damage to his neighbour. In The Darley Main Colliery Co. v. Mitchell 1 Lord Halsbury said: 'It is clear no action would lie for excavation. It is not, therefore, a cause of action; that case Bonomi v. Backhouse (supra) established that it is the damage and not excavation which is the cause of action.'"
